cases.source_title: ESA’s Euclid Space Telescope Finds Universe’s Most Ancient Quasars - NASA Science

candidates.source_quote: Led by ESA (European Space Agency) with contributions from NASA, the Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 of the oldest quasars ever documented.
candidates.standalone_claim: The Euclid space telescope, led by ESA with contributions from NASA, discovered 31 of the oldest quasars ever documented.
candidates.reason: This is a verifiable claim about the discovery made by a specific scientific mission.

candidates.source_quote: The 31 imaged by Euclid include 12 that date to the first 770 million years of the universe.
candidates.standalone_claim: Twelve of the quasars imaged by the Euclid space telescope date to the first 770 million years of the universe.
candidates.reason: This is a specific, quantifiable scientific assertion that can be checked against the study's data.

candidates.source_quote: Two others — the oldest ever documented — formed during the universe’s first 670 million years, and their light has taken some 13 billion light-years to reach Earth.
candidates.standalone_claim: Two of the quasars documented by Euclid formed during the universe's first 670 million years and their light traveled 13 billion light-years to reach Earth.
candidates.reason: This claim provides specific temporal and distance metrics that are verifiable through astronomical data.

candidates.source_quote: Euclid’s findings will help inform plans for NASA’s forthcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which will offer more insights into the mystery of dark energy.
candidates.standalone_claim: Euclid's findings are intended to inform plans for NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
candidates.reason: This describes a future scientific plan and the intended use of research data, which is verifiable as a stated objective.

cases.source_title: NASA Study of Pristine Meteorite Adds to Story of Ancient Asteroids - NASA Science

candidates.source_quote: In a study published Wednesday in the journal Science Advances, researchers found evidence that ancient salty water altered minerals within the meteorite's parent asteroid, preserving unique minerals and a rich inventory of organic compounds.

candidates.source_quote: Its diversity of amino acids and other organic compounds is, comparable to the Murchison meteorite, a nearly 100-kilogram carbonaceous chondrite that fell in Australia in 1969 and became the benchmark for extraterrestrial organic chemistry.
